newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Nov oil trade gap falls 48 pct to $23 mln.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Nov oil trade gap falls 48 pct to $23 mln.

text.p: Peru's oil and derivatives trade deficit was $23 million in November, 48 percent lower than the same month last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Wednesday.
The country's oil and derivatives deficit in the first 11 months was $292 million, off three percent from the same period last year, the bank said in its weekly report.

November's imports of oil and derivatives were $53 million, down from $57 million in the same month last year. Exports in November rose to $31 million, up from $13 million in the same month last year, the bank said.
In the first ten months of the year, imports of oil and derivatives rose 23.9 percent to $625 million. Exports rose 50.7 percent to $333 million, compared with the same period in 1995.
Peru's oil deficit swelled 134 percent to $323.2 million in 1995 compared with $138 million the previous year, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry.
